parts.text: State the conservation law that gives rise to Kirchhoff's second law.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
The potential difference (p.d.) across the two resistors is $V$.

The current in the cell is $I$.
parts.text:
A circuit contains a cell of internal resistance $r$ and two resistors of resistances $R_1$ and $R_2$, as shown in Fig. 5.1.
{{figure:figure_5_1.png}}

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Use Kirchhoff's laws to show that the total resistance $R_T$ of the external circuit is given by
$$\frac{1}{R_T} = \frac{1}{R_1} + \frac{1}{R_2}.$$

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The electromotive force (e.m.f.) of the cell is $1.50\text{ V}$.

When the values of $R_1$ and $R_2$ are $10\Omega$ and $15\Omega$ respectively, the p.d. measured by the voltmeter is $1.38\text{ V}$.

Calculate the internal resistance $r$ of the cell.

parts.text: A third resistor is added in parallel with $R_1$ and $R_2$ in the circuit in Fig. 5.1.
